title: 15: Import GitHub issues with dependencies and provenance
body:
## Specification

[Approved Kiln product specification](https://github.com/VictorGTheCoder/kiln/blob/main/docs/spec.md)

## What to build

Import an existing GitHub backlog into Kiln's ticket planning workflow while preserving issue references and dependencies and keeping approved repository specs authoritative.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A developer can import selected issues with their content, identifiers, URLs, labels, and available blocking relationships.
- [ ] Missing prerequisites and invalid imported dependency graphs are reported before imported work becomes executable.
- [ ] Imported content is reconciled with approved repository specs; divergence is visible and cannot silently overwrite approved requirements.
- [ ] Imported tickets retain their GitHub identity and spec associations through planning and validation.
- [ ] Import is repeatable without creating duplicate local ticket identities and does not start implementation or mutate GitHub issues by itself.
- [ ] Targeted contract verification and deterministic fixtures cover a related issue set, a missing blocker, and divergence from a repository spec.

## Blocked by

- #2: 2: Generate and independently verify tickets from specs

## Spec coverage

User stories: 3, 4, 8.

## Verification approach

Prefer the approved CLI-driven workflow boundary in a temporary Git repository with deterministic agent responses. Add targeted real-provider contract checks or browser checks where the acceptance criteria require them. Verify externally observable behavior rather than internal implementation details.

labels.description: Approved, specified work; start once blocking dependencies are complete.
